problem.title: Tuning Service Mesh Sidecar CPU & Latency
problem.prompt: A Kubernetes payments cluster with 350 services runs Istio Envoy sidecars configured with `requests.cpu: 100m` and `limits.cpu: 200m`. Whenever a deploy triggers xDS route pushes or traffic spikes 2x, p99 latency on healthy pods jumps by 150–400 ms in sawtooth waves, and readiness probes fail. Application CPU is only 25%, yet `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total` on `istio-proxy` hits 65%.

spark.summary: Strict Kubernetes CPU limits on Envoy sidecars trigger Linux CFS quota throttling during mTLS and xDS config bursts, stalling the single-threaded event loop and freezing all pod traffic.
spark.keyTakeaway: Remove hard CPU limits on Istio/Envoy sidecars (keep CPU requests), isolate xDS updates via Sidecar CRDs, and tune Envoy worker concurrency.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** In a 350-service Istio cluster (`1,400` endpoints pushed to every pod), setting `limits.cpu: 200m` on `istio-proxy` gives Envoy only `20 ms` of CPU time per `100 ms` Linux CFS quota period (`cpu.cfs_period_us = 100000`).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 200m CPU Limit Stalls Envoy Event Loop for 80ms Every 100ms Period (App (25% CPU) -> Envoy (200m limit) -> Linux CFS (100ms) -> istiod (xDS)); requests.cpu (No Limit) + Sidecar CRD + concurrency=2 (istiod Control Plane -> istio-proxy (concurrency=2) -> Linux CFS cpu.shares -> Payments App (25% CPU)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** A 5-minute Grafana CPU graph showing `80m` average hides sub-100 ms micro-bursts during mTLS handshakes and xDS reloads. Eliminate `150–400 ms` CFS stalls and shrink proxy memory across 350 services: **Remove `limits.cpu`, Keep `requests.cpu: 200m`**: Without `limits.cpu`, Linux CFS does not.

**Failure Modes & Application:** CFS quota awareness and xDS scoping are essential for large multi-tenant meshes: **Istio / Linkerd Production Clusters**: Standardizes no-CPU-limit Burstable QoS for latency-sensitive proxies.

learningJourney.title: Why Kubernetes 200m CPU limits freeze Envoy sidecars for 90 ms
learningJourney.explanation: In a 350-service Istio cluster (`1,400` endpoints pushed to every pod), setting `limits.cpu: 200m` on `istio-proxy` gives Envoy only `20 ms` of CPU time per `100 ms` Linux CFS quota period (`cpu.cfs_period_us = 100000`). If 2 Envoy worker threads burn `10 ms` each during an mTLS handshake or xDS push, CFS **freezes the entire sidecar for the remaining 80–90 ms**.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Why Kubernetes 200m CPU limits freeze Envoy sidecars for 90 ms works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: 150–400 ms sawtooth p99 latency waves and xDS memory bloat
learningJourney.explanation:
Throttled Envoy sidecars stall healthy applications even when app CPU is only `25%`:

1. **Sawtooth Latency Waves**: Every multi-hop call stacks `80–90 ms` CFS quota pauses (`150–400 ms` p99 spikes) and fails readiness probes.
2. **Mesh-Wide xDS Bloat**: Without `Sidecar` CRDs, all 350 services x 1,400 endpoints are parsed by every proxy, wasting hundreds of MBs of RAM on nodes already at `72%` memory.

learningJourney.title: Why sizing CPU limits from 5-min averages and concurrency=0 fails
learningJourney.explanation: A 5-minute Grafana CPU graph showing `80m` average hides sub-100 ms micro-bursts during mTLS handshakes and xDS reloads. Leaving Envoy `concurrency: 0` on 64-core nodes also spawns `64` worker threads, each consuming memory and contending for the `200m` CFS quota.
learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why sizing CPU limits from 5-min averages and concurrency=0 fails under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Drop CPU Limits, Scope Sidecar CRDs, Tune Concurrency
learningJourney.explanation:
Eliminate `150–400 ms` CFS stalls and shrink proxy memory across 350 services:

- **Remove `limits.cpu`, Keep `requests.cpu: 200m`**: Without `limits.cpu`, Linux CFS does not hard-throttle bursts onto idle node CPU, while `cpu.shares` still protects co-located app containers under node contention.
- **Namespace `Sidecar` CRDs**: Restrict each pod's `egress.hosts` to only its declared dependencies (`./*`, `istio-system/*`), cutting xDS config size, parse CPU, and Envoy RAM by `80–95%`.
- **Set `proxyMetadata` / `concurrency: 2`**: Bound Envoy worker threads to `2` instead of `0` (all host cores) to slash per-thread memory and lock contention.

cards.detail: Dropping limits.cpu removes the 100ms hard quota wall while cpu.shares prevents noisy neighbors.

cards.detail: Prunes 1,400 cluster-wide endpoints down to only the namespace's actual egress targets.

cards.detail: Prevents Envoy from spawning 64 threads on large nodes, saving RAM at 72% node utilization.

learningJourney.title: Where service mesh resource tuning is critical in Kubernetes
learningJourney.explanation:
CFS quota awareness and xDS scoping are essential for large multi-tenant meshes:

- **Istio / Linkerd Production Clusters**: Standardizes no-CPU-limit Burstable QoS for latency-sensitive proxies.
- **Zero-Trust mTLS Payments Fleets**: Keeps TLS handshakes sub-millisecond during pod autoscaling.
- **Large Multi-Namespace Meshes**: Prevents `O(N^2)` xDS config push storms across 300+ services.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does a `200m` Kubernetes CPU limit cause 80-90 ms latency stalls on an Envoy sidecar even when total node CPU is under 30%?

options.text: Linux CFS enforces CPU limits in 100ms windows (20ms quota for 200m); once 2 Envoy threads burn 20ms in a burst, CFS freezes the container until the next 100ms period
options.feedback: Correct: CFS hard quota throttles micro-bursts regardless of idle CPU on the host.

options.text: Envoy disables mTLS whenever CPU limits are below 500m
options.feedback: mTLS stays active, which is why handshake bursts trigger CFS throttling.

options.text: Kubernetes Sidecar CRDs require 1 full CPU core to parse YAML
options.feedback: Sidecar CRDs actually *reduce* Envoy xDS CPU and memory by 80-95%.

_problemQuestions.prompt: A user edits their bio and refreshes the page, only to see the old bio for 2 seconds because the read hit a lagging replica. Which consistency guarantee was violated?

options.explanation: Read-Your-Writes ensures a client always observes its own completed writes.
The write was durable on the primary; the replica simply lagged.
Atomicity governs all-or-nothing commit, not cross-replica visibility.

_problemQuestions.prompt: Why does placing `request_timestamp` at the very beginning of a 3,000-token system prompt hurt latency and cost?

options.explanation: BPE still tokenizes the text normally.

options.text: It invalidates prefix/KV caching for all subsequent 3,000 tokens on every request
options.explanation: Correct! Prefix KV caching requires an exact token match from index 0 onward.
Output length is unaffected; Prefill cache reuse is what breaks.
